phrase: AI agents can now shop, message, and chat on your behalf. A new study found they still struggle with everyday life.
phraseAlternatives: A social network put its AI agent inside everyone's private messages this week. A new benchmark says such agents still struggle with ordinary tasks.
This week, AI agents moved into shopping apps and group chats. A study found they are still bad at everyday life.
AI agents can now book, buy, and chat for you. They still can't reliably manage a simple daily task.
alt: A small robot with arms thrown up in surprise trips over a thin wire just past a round, speech-bubble-shaped doorway, shopping-bag contents flying from its side, while a person with arms crossed sits in a chair nearby, a speech bubble reading "Not again."

brief.concept: A small AI agent struts proudly through a messaging app's round doorway, arms full of shopping bags, only to trip over an ordinary wire just past the threshold, spilling everything.
brief.metaphor: Confidence outruns competence: the agent conquers the doorway into daily life, then stumbles on the simplest step just inside it.

brief.composition: Simple vector scene, left to right: a small AI robot strides through a round, speech-bubble-shaped doorway with shopping bags in hand, chest out, confident. Just past the threshold its foot catches a low wire; its body is already tipping forward, bags' contents flying into the air. To the right, a human sits in a plain armchair, arms crossed, one eyebrow raised, unimpressed. Flat blue-and-pink riso shapes, thick outlines, warm cream paper, with the spilling bag as the single overprinted highlight marking the joke.
brief.alt: A small robot confidently marches through a speech-bubble-shaped doorway carrying shopping bags, then trips over a low wire just beyond it, spilling the bags' contents, while a human sits in a chair watching with arms crossed.
